description: Files the program CREATES while running (saves, caches, logs), declared by project_ops.declare_artifacts AFTER the code has been written and persisted to architecture.transient_files. These are deleted between behavioural test sessions so one test's leftover state cannot contaminate the next. This is deliberately NOT asked at design time: before the code exists the answer is a guess, and on 2026-07-29 the guess was ['save.json', '*.autosave.json'] for a program that wrote game_state.json — the flush matched nothing 22 times and 91% of test sessions resumed mid-run.

transient_files.description: One entry per file or glob the program writes at runtime. Empty array is a valid, meaningful answer: it asserts the program writes nothing. NEVER list input data files (content definitions, config, world data) — only program-generated output.

pattern.description: Exact filename or fnmatch glob, relative to the project root. Must be the name the CODE actually writes, read off the source — not a plausible-sounding name. Relative only: a leading / or ~ or any .. is rejected downstream.

written_by.description: Where in the source this file is written — the module, and the constant or call that names it (e.g. "main.py: SAVE_FILE = 'game_state.json', written by save_state() on exit"). REQUIRED: citing the write site is what forces the pattern to be read rather than guessed, and it is the audit trail when a later flush deletes the file.

transient_files.written_by: main.py: SAVE_FILE = 'game_state.json'; save_state(engine.state, SAVE_FILE) on exit, and os.remove(SAVE_FILE) on win/death
